title: Decide whether to build, buy or partner
summary: Build what makes you different, and buy or partner for the rest. Make the choice on purpose for each major capability, including AI.

beginner: List the capabilities your bets need.
Mark which ones make you different from competitors.
For the others, find out what you could buy or use from a partner.
Compare total cost over several years, not just the first year.
Write down the choice and the reason for each capability.
intermediate: Include running, support and switching costs in the comparison.
Check data, security and lock-in risks for bought or partner options.
For AI, compare using an existing model, adapting one and building your own.
experienced: Set build, buy and partner principles across the portfolio.
Review past choices as markets change: today's differentiator can become a commodity.
Negotiate partnerships that keep your options open.

canDelegateTo.task: Assess technical fit and integration effort
Review contracts, data and lock-in risks

toolExamples.google-docs: Compare options on cost, time, risk and fit in one table.
toolExamples.confluence: Record each decision and its reason.

definitionOfDone: Each major capability has a build, buy or partner decision
pitfalls: Buying a package and then customising it heavily
